posts.title: The Download: why AI’s latest breakthroughs and fears may be more hype than reality
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Don’t be fooled by this summer of AI hype  —Timnit Gebru, executive director of the Distributed AI Research Institute (DAIR), and Emily M. Bender, professor of linguistics at the University of…
bullets: AMD has officially joined the $1 trillion market cap club, driven by a 180% surge in share price fueled by massive demand for AI-specific hardware.
Regulatory pressure is mounting as 22 nations push for a global AI oversight body, while Texas and California implement new restrictions on data center power and water consumption.
Meta's AI agent 'Muse' has reached the top of the US App Store, though it faces significant security risks, including a zero-day vulnerability and exclusion from Amazon's platform.
Experts warn that the current AI landscape is heavily influenced by commercial incentives to overstate capabilities, potentially misdirecting both public perception and policy decisions.

posts.title: CATL begins trial cell production at planned 100 GWh Hungary plant
posts.summary:
The Hungarian plant will become CATL's largest production base outside China once all facilities are ready.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: CATL has commenced trial battery cell production at its Debrecen plant in Hungary, utilizing its first two production lines to validate manufacturing processes.
Once fully operational, the facility is designed for a 100 GWh capacity, positioning it as CATL's largest production base outside of China.
The successful start of trial operations follows the receipt of all necessary environmental and occupancy permits, marking a critical step in localizing supply for European automakers.
